'''Yorkshire pudding''' is a dish popular across the UK but originating in the county of Yorkshire in England. It's traditionally eaten with beef or lamb with vegetables.

== Ingredients ==
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) unbleached [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|white flour]]
* 1 cup (240 g) [[Cookbook:Whole Wheat Flour|whole wheat pastry flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* Ener-G egg replacer equivalent of 2 eggs
* 1 cup (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Nondairy Milk|soy milk]]
* 1 cup (240 ml) very cold water
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] vegan [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], melted

== Procedure ==
# Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (210°C). 
# In a mixing bowl, combine the flours and salt. Make a well in the center and add the egg replacer mixture. Stir together until just combined, then add the soy milk and water, a bit at a time. Stir until smooth, but don’t overbeat. 
# Swirl the melted margarine around a shallow, 9x13-inch (22-32 cm) [[Cookbook:Baking Pan|baking pan]]. Pour out any excess and reserve. Pour the batter into the pan and pour any remaining margarine over the top.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 20 minutes, or until golden on top and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean. Let cool, then cut into squares to serve.
